title: A gate needs enough items
statement: A mastery gate needs enough items to mean anything, so check what its bar demands at each test's real length: on four or five items, 90% means a perfect score.
example: On a five-item test one wrong answer is 80%, under a 90% bar.
detail: An evaluation of a live Grade 3 course found two tests of 4-5 items that could not be gated at 90% (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0058-eval-reading-explorers-g3-allqtypes.qmd`), and the staged item standard says a test of fewer than 5 items cannot certify mastery at 90%, since 1 wrong is 80% on a 5-item test (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/item-quality.md`); the evaluator gap list names the same trap (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0093-evaluator-gap-analysis-inceptbench-academics-2026-07-09.qmd`). In the same course, lessons set up as adaptive gates were single-question tests, and because the adaptive score is incremental, one right answer took it from 0 to 14, not 100, so the lesson looped on the same question (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0021-powerpath100-course-shape-rootcause.qmd`). Work it out again whenever items are removed. A few items can guide practice but not a mastery call, and on four or five items a 90% bar demands a perfect score.
against: How many items are enough needs its own source: one audit's 15-item bank floor turned out to be an arbitrary constant in the audit script itself, and the real platform floor was 8 (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0235-g5-course-build-pipeline-2026-06-23-to-06-30.qmd`). The item counts assume well-constructed items with good discrimination; poorly written items shorten a test's effective length. the project's routing rules define mastery through controlled evidence and downstream risk rather than a global raw 90% (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0164-g3-v2-feedback-agent-routing.qmd`, line 88).

evidence.quote: **A test with <5 items cannot certify mastery at 90%** (1 wrong = 80% on a 5-item test; un-gateable on a 4-item test). Gate tests carry **enough items** for a 90% threshold to be meaningful.
two 4-5 item tests are un-gateable (no "90% of 4"); no three-state retry / parallel forms.
PowerPath scoring is **incremental**: one correct answer from 0 → score **14, not 100**.
gate-arithmetic trap where small tests make 90 percent require a perfect score;
an arbitrary `>=15` bank-depth constant hardcoded in `audit_compliance.py` itself … the real platform/publisher floor is 8.
a 5-item MCQ quiz is useful for retrieval practice and rough formative diagnosis but is too unreliable for mastery decisions.
A 10–15 item assessment begins to support cautious inferences about whether a student has grasped the core content.
A 20–30 item assessment, with a well-designed blueprint, can support summative judgments about attainment across a domain.
These numbers assume well-constructed items with good discrimination; poorly written items reduce effective test length.
leak-purge shrank tests to 5–9 items → 90% gate = perfect-score-only (ceil(0.9n)=n for n≤9)
**Arithmetic traps hide in small n.** ceil(0.9×n) = n for n ≤ 9: a 90% gate on a ≤9-item test demands a perfect score.
Gate arithmetic note: at 22 items, ceil(0.9×22)=20 → the gate tolerates 2 misses; no G5-style perfect-score trap.
